_about: Provider-message corpus for quota detection.
Detection is the one judgement this program makes on its own account: a
`quota_exhausted` verdict hops the job AND opens a five-hour breaker on a
seat, across every repository on the machine. quota.py's own docstring
states the bias -- calling a real wall `other` costs one attempt, calling a
healthy seat a wall hides a working provider for an afternoon, silently.
So the corpus is weighted the way the risk is. The positives are shapes; the
negatives are the point, and most of them are one class: AN AGENT DOING
ORDINARY WORK ON RATE-LIMITING CODE EMITS EXACTLY THE STRINGS THIS TABLE
MATCHES. Review a limiter, write a 429 handler, grep for RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED
-- the words land in the agent's own output, and if that invocation also
exits non-zero for some unrelated reason, the transcript is what gets
classified.
These are representative shapes, not a capture log. They are written from
provider error formats and from what an agent's transcript looks like; none
is claimed to be a verbatim recording of a specific provider on a specific
day. That is why `via` matters more than exact wording: it says WHERE in a
CLI's output the text arrived, which is the part detection actually turns on.
via:
stderr      the CLI's own error stream -- where a refusal normally lands
stdout      plain-text CLI, everything on one stream (codex, gemini)
result      inside a JSON envelope's `result` field: THE AGENT'S OWN PROSE,
never the provider speaking
error_code  a JSON envelope's `error.code` -- a structured refusal
rather than prose. NOT herdr: herdr's AgentInfo carries no
error field, and its pane path classifies nothing at all.
reset: null = must carry no reopen time. A number = seconds after T0.
"some" = must parse to something, value not pinned here.
`wrong: true` marks a case detection gets WRONG today. They are asserted
against current behaviour so the suite stays honest rather than aspirational,
and their count is pinned separately -- fix one and that test fails, telling
you to move it. See test_failover.TestProviderMessageCorpus.
## Where real ones come from: corpus-capture.jsonl
The cases above are shapes, and they are shapes because collecting real
provider walls was a chore nobody was going to do. So runs now do it as
exhaust: every time a live run classifies a message as `quota_exhausted`,
adg/corpus.py appends one JSON line to
$XDG_STATE_HOME/agent-delegation/corpus-capture.jsonl -- the text the
PATTERN TABLE saw (not what the log kept; on the local path those differ),
the verdict, the reset time as parsed, and which adapter, seat and model
were involved. Capture cannot fail a run: it is wrapped, its result is
ignored, and an unwritable state directory loses the line and nothing else.
REDACTION IS BEST-EFFORT. Stdlib regex strips home-directory paths, email
addresses and API-key-shaped strings before the line is written. It is
pattern matching over text this program did not write, so a secret in a
shape adg/corpus.py does not list will be in that file. Nothing here
uploads it. Read a line before you paste it anywhere.
Promotion is BY HAND and stays that way. Nothing reads the capture file
back, and no test ingests it: a case earns its place in `cases` once a
human has decided what it proves, and auto-ingesting would let a corpus
that is supposed to pin behaviour be written by the behaviour it pins.
To promote one:
1. Read the line. Confirm the redaction did its job on THIS text.
2. Write a case: `kind` is the record's `kind`; `text` is its `text`;
`expect` is its `verdict`.
3. Decide `via` yourself -- the record does not carry it, because after
the fact nothing knows which stream the text arrived on. It is the
part detection most turns on, so guessing it makes the case worse
than absent. If you cannot tell, do not promote the line.
4. Turn `reset_in_s` into `{T0+N}` inside `text` and put N in `reset`,
or `null` when nothing was parsed, or "some" when the value is not
worth pinning.
5. Run the suite. A promoted case that fails is a detection bug, and it
belongs here marked `wrong: true` until somebody fixes it.
